beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: In the beginning there was a garden, and in the garden, peace. People and God walking together in the cool of the day, with nothing to hide and nothing to fear.

timing.text: In the beginning there was a garden, and in the garden, peace.
People and God walking together in the cool of the day, with nothing to hide and nothing to fear.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: There was only one thing they were asked not to do. And, as people do, they did it anyway — reaching for the one thing that was not theirs, hoping it would make them more than they were.

timing.text: There was only one thing they were asked not to do.
And, as people do, they did it anyway — reaching for the one thing that was not theirs, hoping it would make them more than they were.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And everything changed. For the first time they felt shame. They saw themselves, and did not like what they saw, and scrambled to cover up, hiding from each other.

timing.text: And everything changed.
For the first time they felt shame.
They saw themselves, and did not like what they saw, and scrambled to cover up, hiding from each other.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And then they heard him coming — the warm presence of God moving through the garden in the cool of the evening, the way he always had. And this time, they ran and hid themselves among the trees.

timing.text: And then they heard him coming — the warm presence of God moving through the garden in the cool of the evening, the way he always had.
And this time, they ran and hid themselves among the trees.
Where art thou?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Where are you. Not, what have you done. Not, how dare you. Where are you — the cry of a Father looking for a child who is hiding. He knew exactly where they were. He asked so they would come out. And, trembling, the man answered.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself.

timing.text: I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That is the whole of it. Not defiance — fear. Shame has never once made a person run toward God. It makes them run behind a tree.

timing.text: That is the whole of it.
Not defiance — fear.
Shame has never once made a person run toward God.
It makes them run behind a tree.

beats.speaker: god
beats.text: What is this that thou hast done?

timing.text: What is this that thou hast done?

beats.speaker: woman
beats.text: The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.

timing.text: The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: I was deceived, she said, and I ate. No excuses left — just the truth, spoken out loud at last. There were consequences; there always are. The easy garden was behind them now, and a hard world lay ahead. They stood there, ashamed, waiting for the end of everything.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And instead, God did something they never expected. He made them clothes. With his own care he covered their shame — better coverings than the leaves they had grabbed for themselves — because they could not fix what they had broken, and he would not leave them exposed.

timing.text: And instead, God did something they never expected.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Then he sent them out into the wide world — but not naked, and not alone, and not without a promise. Clothed by the very One they had run from.

timing.text: Then he sent them out into the wide world — but not naked, and not alone, and not without a promise.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That is the God of the very first story. Not one who waits for you to clean yourself up and come find him. One who comes walking through the garden in the cool of the evening, calling, still calling — where are you? — because he wants you back.

card.text: The first thing God said to hiding people was not a scolding — it was, where are you? He still comes seeking, and still covers the shame we cannot cover ourselves. Where are you hiding, that he is gently calling you out of?
